claim: Hepatitis E virus (HEV) is responsible for over 20 million infections annually.
source: Hepatitis E virus (HEV) has a global disease burden of over 20 million cases per annum, leading to approximately 70,000 fatalities (Rein et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Rein et al., 2012.

claim: HEV causes approximately 70,000 fatalities annually.
source: Hepatitis E virus (HEV) has a global disease burden of over 20 million cases per annum, leading to approximately 70,000 fatalities (Rein et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Rein et al., 2012.

claim: Pregnant women experience a close to 30% mortality rate from HEV in the third trimester.
source: This burden is especially pronounced in immunocompromised individuals and pregnant women, the latter of whom experience a close to 30% mortality rate in the third trimester (Khuroo and Kamili, 2003)
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Khuroo and Kamili, 2003.

claim: HEV causes approximately 3000 stillbirths.
source: and/or approximately 3000 stillbirths (Rein et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Rein et al., 2012.

claim: A prophylactic HEV vaccine is currently only licensed in China.
source: HEV infection can be prevented with a prophylactic vaccine which is currently only licensed in China.
evidence: The claim is stated directly in the text without supporting data or citation.

claim: HEV treatment is limited to ribavirin and pegylated type I interferon.
source: Presently, treatment is limited to ribavirin (RBV; Lee and Hung, 2014) and pegylated type I interferon (IFN; Kamar et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Lee and Hung, 2014 and Kamar et al., 2010.

claim: Ribavirin is teratogenic and cannot be administered during pregnancy.
source: However, these therapies are plagued with considerable side effects, as RBV is teratogenic and thus cannot be administered during pregnancy
evidence: The claim is stated as established knowledge about ribavirin.

claim: IFN therapy can lead to transplant rejection in organ transplant recipients.
source: and IFN therapy can lead to transplant rejection in organ transplant recipients (Haagsma et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Haagsma et al., 2010.

claim: HEV strains with fitness-enhancing mutations have been identified in patients showing clinical resistance to RBV treatment.
source: Furthermore, HEV strains with fitness-enhancing mutations have been identified in patients showing clinical resistance to RBV treatment (Todt et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Todt et al., 2018.

claim: HEV is a (+) ssRNA virus in the Orthohepevirus genus in the Hepeviridae family of viruses.
source: HEV is a (+) ssRNA virus in the Orthohepevirus genus in the Hepeviridae family of viruses (Smith et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Smith et al., 2014.

claim: The HEV genome has a 5'-methylated cap and a 3'-poly (A) tail.
source: The genome of HEV has a 5'-methylated cap and a 3'-poly (A) tail and is composed of three partially overlapping open reading frames (ORFs).
evidence: The claim is stated as established knowledge about HEV genome structure.

claim: The HEV genome is composed of three partially overlapping open reading frames (ORFs).
source: The genome of HEV has a 5'-methylated cap and a 3'-poly (A) tail and is composed of three partially overlapping open reading frames (ORFs).
evidence: The claim is stated as established knowledge about HEV genome structure.

claim: ORF1 encodes the viral replicase.
source: ORF1 encodes the viral replicase (Koonin et al., 1992)
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Koonin et al., 1992.

claim: ORF2 encodes the capsid protein.
source: ORF2 encodes the capsid protein (Reyes et al., 1993; Tam et al., 1991)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Reyes et al., 1993 and Tam et al., 1991.

claim: ORF3 encodes a viroporin necessary for viral egress.
source: and ORF3 encodes a viroporin necessary for viral egress (Ding et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Ding et al., 2017.

claim: HEV ORF1 has been organized into seven domains based on prior bioinformatic analysis.
source: ORF1 has been organized into seven domains based on prior bioinformatic analysis (Figure 1A; Koonin et al., 1992)
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Koonin et al., 1992 and reference to Figure 1A.

claim: Four domains of HEV ORF1 have been functionally characterized: the methyltransferase, macrodomain, helicase, and RNA-dependent RNA polymerase.
source: only four of which have been functionally characterized in some detail: namely the methyltransferase (Magden et al., 2001), macrodomain (Parvez, 2015), helicase (Devhare et al., 2014; Karpe and Lole, 2010), and RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp; Koonin, 1991; van der Heijden and Bol, 2002).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to studies characterizing each domain.

claim: Several groups have disagreed on the presence of protease activity in the putative papain-like cysteine protease (pPCP) domain.
source: Of the remaining domains of HEV ORF1, the putative papain-like cysteine protease (pPCP) has been the subject of some debate; several groups assessing the functionality of this region have disagreed on the presence of protease activity (Ansari et al., 2000; Kanade et al., 2018; Karpe and Lole, 2011; Paliwal et al., 2014; Parvez, 2013; Parvez and Khan, 2014; Perttilä et al., 2013; Ropp et al., 2000; Sehgal et al., 2006; Suppiah et al., 2011)
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to studies with conflicting results.

claim: Mutations in the core six of eight highly conserved cysteines within the pPCP render Kc1/p6 HEV replication incompetent.
source: We were able to demonstrate that mutations in the core six of the eight highly conserved cysteines within the pPCP, as well as the heterogenous residue at position 590, renders Kc1/p6 HEV replication incompetent.
evidence: The claim is stated as a result from the study's experiments.

claim: The putative catalytic cysteine in the HEV pPCP renders HEV in three additional genotypes replication incompetent.
source: We were also able to show that the putative catalytic cysteine in the HEV pPCP renders HEV in three additional genotypes replication incompetent.
evidence: The claim is stated as a result from the study's experiments.

claim: Transfection of wild type Kc1/p6 Gluc into naïve Huh7.5 human hepatoma cells led to a ca. 34,000-fold increase in luminescence over mock cells.
source: Transfection of the wild type (wt) Kc1/p6 Gluc into naïve Huh7.5 human hepatoma cells led to a ca. 34,000-fold increase in luminescence over mock cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data described in the text.

claim: Transfection of a polymerase deficient genome harboring a mutation in the GDD motif of the RdRp did not augment Gluc activity.
source: Transfection of a polymerase deficient genome harboring a mutation in the highly conserved catalytic triad (GDD motif of the RdRp (deemed pol [-])) expectedly did not augment Gluc activity (Figure 1B–C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B-C.

claim: Genomes harboring mutations in the C483 and/or Y590 positions were incapable of establishing stable replication.
source: Notably, genomes harboring mutations in the C483 and/or Y590 positions were incapable of establishing stable replication (Figure 1B–C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B-C.

claim: HEV RNA replication was severely impaired in SAR55, SHEV3, and TW6196E genomes harboring the C483A mutation.
source: In line with our observations using Kc1/p6 replicon, HEV RNA replication was severely impaired in SAR55, SHEV3, and TW6196E genomes harboring the C483A mutation (Figure 1D–G).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D-G.

claim: Encoding the alternate cysteine codon had a mild negative effect on viral replication efficiency.
source: These analyses demonstrated that encoding the alternate cysteine had a mild negative affect on viral replication efficiency, while any alanine codon usage brought replication levels down to those of the Pol (-) mutant (Figure 1H)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1H.

claim: Any alanine codon usage at position C483 brought replication levels down to those of the Pol (-) mutant.
source: These analyses demonstrated that encoding the alternate cysteine had a mild negative affect on viral replication efficiency, while any alanine codon usage brought replication levels down to those of the Pol (-) mutant (Figure 1H)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1H.

claim: The C483A deficiency primarily lies in protein folding or function rather than RNA folding.
source: suggesting that the deficiency primarily lies in protein folding or function.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the codon substitution experiments showing amino acid but not codon-specific effects.

claim: Cells expressing a mutant form of ORF1 demonstrate a deleterious effect on WT replicon replication, likely due to competitive inhibitory binding of the mutant protein with the replicon RNA.
source: Notably, when the mock signal fold change over WT luciferase signal was examined, cells expressing a mutant form of ORF1 demonstrate a deleterious effect on WT replicon replication, likely due to competitive inhibitory binding of the mutant protein with the replicon RNA (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B and includes a speculative explanation.

claim: Impairments in viral genome replication due to the pol (-) or C483A mutations could be rescued in trans by expression of WT ORF1.
source: Impairments in viral genome replication due to the pol (-) or C483A mutations could be rescued in trans by expression of WT ORF1 near to levels of those following transfection of WT replicon RNA (Figure 2D–E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D-E.

claim: Expression of the pPCP alone failed to restore replication of Kc1/p6 Gluc C483A.
source: Of note, expression of the pPCP failed to restore replication of Kc1/p6 Gluc C483A, suggesting that the functions of this region of ORF1 are not adequately maintained outside of the context of the ORF1 polyprotein.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from the transcomplementation assay.

claim: The functions of the pPCP region of ORF1 are not adequately maintained outside of the context of the ORF1 polyprotein.
source: Of note, expression of the pPCP failed to restore replication of Kc1/p6 Gluc C483A, suggesting that the functions of this region of ORF1 are not adequately maintained outside of the context of the ORF1 polyprotein.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the failure of pPCP alone to rescue replication.

claim: An octa-cysteine motif is highly conserved across all HEV genotypes.
source: We examined the pPCP sequences across all eight known HEV genotypes (Figure 1—figure supplement 1) and noticed an octa-cysteine motif highly conserved across all HEV genotypes (Figure 3A).
evidence: The claim is supported by sequence analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1 and Figure 3A.

claim: The core hexa-cysteine motif encompassing cysteines 457–483 in SAR55 genotype 1 HEV were necessary for viral replication.
source: Previous work has shown the core hexa-cysteine motif encompassing cysteines 457–483 in SAR55 genotype 1 HEV were necessary for viral replication (Parvez, 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Parvez, 2013.

claim: Of the eight conserved cysteines, only the core six that form a CxC[x11]CC[x8]CxC hexa-cysteine motif are vital for viral replication.
source: We noticed that of the eight conserved cysteines, only the core six that form a CxC[x11]CC[x8]CxC hexa-cysteine motif are vital for viral replication, with the first cysteine at position C434 being completely dispensable for replication, and the final cysteine at position C563 having a slight detriment to replication when mutated to alanine (Figure 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The first cysteine at position C434 is completely dispensable for replication.
source: We noticed that of the eight conserved cysteines, only the core six that form a CxC[x11]CC[x8]CxC hexa-cysteine motif are vital for viral replication, with the first cysteine at position C434 being completely dispensable for replication, and the final cysteine at position C563 having a slight detriment to replication when mutated to alanine (Figure 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The final cysteine at position C563 has a slight detriment to replication when mutated to alanine.
source: We noticed that of the eight conserved cysteines, only the core six that form a CxC[x11]CC[x8]CxC hexa-cysteine motif are vital for viral replication, with the first cysteine at position C434 being completely dispensable for replication, and the final cysteine at position C563 having a slight detriment to replication when mutated to alanine (Figure 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Triplicates containing any of the conserved cysteines were indispensable for viral replication.
source: Notably, triplicates containing any of the conserved cysteines, as well as the variable amino acid at position 590 were indispensable for viral replication, despite point mutations at positions C434 and C563 being tolerated (Figure 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B and Figure 3C.

claim: The amino acid stretches 55–63 and 73–81 directly downstream of the hexa-cysteine motif tolerate mutagenesis quite well.
source: Additionally, the amino acid stretches 55–63 and 73–81 directly downstream of the hexa-cysteine motif tolerate mutagenesis quite well, suggesting a possible structural/linker function of these amino acids
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from the alanine scanning mutagenesis and includes an inference about function.

claim: Relaxing the hexa-cysteine motif search criteria to (±) 1 for each stretch of [x] brought forth 26 proteins with known functions, enriched for proteins with divalent metal ion binding activity.
source: Relaxing the criteria to (±) 1 for each of the stretches of [x] (CxC[x](10–12)CC[x](7–9)CxC) brought forth 26 proteins with known functions (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A), enriched for proteins with divalent metal ion binding activity (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by bioinformatic analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The pPCP region within HEV is necessary for metal ion coordination.
source: We hypothesized that this region within the pPCP is necessary for metal ion coordination.
evidence: The claim is stated as a hypothesis based on bioinformatic analysis.

claim: AlphaFold prediction revealed varying levels of confidence throughout the entirety of ORF1, and importantly, low confidence throughout much of the pPCP.
source: This analysis revealed varying levels of confidence throughout the entirety of ORF1, and importantly, low confidence throughout much of the pPCP.
evidence: The claim is supported by analysis of AlphaFold pLDDT scores.

claim: The pPCP alone averages a pLDDT score of 65.92, and the pPCP within the context of ORF1 scores a slightly better average of 66.05.
source: We further looked at how AlphaFold predicts the pPCP outside of the context of ORF1 and found that the pLDDT averages are very similar (Figure 4C), with the pPCP alone averaging a pLDDT score of 65.92, and the pPCP within the context of ORF1 scoring a slightly better average of 66.05.
evidence: The claim is supported by AlphaFold pLDDT score analysis shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Alignment of 6NU9 with the corresponding region of Kc1/p6 ORF1 shows high local alignment identity, with the average distance of this superimposition aligning at 0.67 Å.
source: Alignment of 6NU9 with the corresponding region of Kc1/p6 ORF1 shows high local alignment identity, with the average distance of this superimposition aligning at 0.67 Å (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by structural alignment data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Alignment of the amphipathic RdRp 'thumb' domain shows incredibly high local alignment identity with a 0.48 Å average differential.
source: Alignment of the amphipathic RdRp 'thumb' domain similarly shows incredibly high local alignment identity with a 0.48 Å average differential (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by structural alignment data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: AlphaFold was able to fold the HAV protease with very high confidence, with an average pLDDT score of 97.14 across the entirety of the prediction.
source: Interestingly, AlphaFold was able to fold the HAV protease with very high confidence, with an average pLDDT score of 97.14 across the entirety of the prediction, giving high confidence of interpretation to both the amino acid backbones and side chain chains (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by AlphaFold pLDDT score analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The majority of the predicted alpha-helices and beta-sheets in the pPCP do not tolerate mutations well.
source: We found that the majority of the predicted alpha-helices and beta-sheets do not tolerate mutations well, while the majority of the tolerated mutants lie within predicted regions of disorder (Figure 4D; Video 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by analysis of alanine scanning mutagenesis data overlaid on AlphaFold predictions shown in Figure 4D and Video 1.

claim: The majority of the tolerated mutants lie within predicted regions of disorder.
source: We found that the majority of the predicted alpha-helices and beta-sheets do not tolerate mutations well, while the majority of the tolerated mutants lie within predicted regions of disorder (Figure 4D; Video 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by analysis of alanine scanning mutagenesis data overlaid on AlphaFold predictions shown in Figure 4D and Video 1.

claim: The HEV ORF1 pPCP domain does not possess the necessary secondary structure of a protease.
source: AlphaFold is able to predict the structure of a known viral protease with high confidence, suggesting further that the HEV pPCP domain does not possess the necessary secondary structure of a protease.
evidence: The claim is inferred from comparing AlphaFold's high confidence prediction of HAV protease with low confidence prediction of HEV pPCP.

claim: A novel pseudo-zinc-finger is formed by the amino acids underlying the HEV hexa-cysteine motif.
source: Upon inspection of the best ranked models for each of these versions of ORF1 (WT, C483A, and C563A), we noticed a novel pseudo-zinc-finger formed by the amino acids underlying the HEV hexa-cysteine motif, despite the low pLDDT scores within this region (Figure 5A, left; Videos 2–4, respectively).
evidence: The claim is supported by AlphaFold structural predictions shown in Figure 5A and Videos 2-4.

claim: Mutation of C483A, but not C563A, is predicted to disrupt the molecular architecture of the pseudo-zinc-finger.
source: Mutation of C483A, but not C563A, is predicted to disrupt the molecular architecture of this pseudo-zinc-finger; however, mutation of either causes a relaxation of several predicted bond lengths to beyond biological relevance (Zheng et al., 2008; Figure 5—figure supplement 1, Videos 2–3).
evidence: The claim is supported by AlphaFold structural predictions shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1 and Videos 2-3, with citation to Zheng et al., 2008 for biological relevance criteria.

claim: Mutation of either C483A or C563A causes a relaxation of several predicted bond lengths to beyond biological relevance.
source: Mutation of C483A, but not C563A, is predicted to disrupt the molecular architecture of this pseudo-zinc-finger; however, mutation of either causes a relaxation of several predicted bond lengths to beyond biological relevance (Zheng et al., 2008; Figure 5—figure supplement 1, Videos 2–3).
evidence: The claim is supported by AlphaFold structural predictions shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1 and Videos 2-3, with citation to Zheng et al., 2008 for biological relevance criteria.

claim: Cysteine side chain residues at positions 457 and 459 are predicted to form a potential tetrahedral divalent ion binding pocket with D248 and H249 in the upstream Y-domain.
source: Cysteine side chain residues at positions 457 and 459 at the end of the predicted beta sheet leading into the pseudo-zinc-finger were shown to be projecting into inter-domain space. These residues are predicted to form a potential tetrahedral divalent ion binding pocket (Laitaoja et al., 2013) with D248 and H249 in the upstream Y-domain (Figure 5A, middle)
evidence: The claim is supported by AlphaFold structural predictions shown in Figure 5A, with citation to Laitaoja et al., 2013 for tetrahedral binding pocket characteristics.

claim: D248 was dispensable for viral replication while H249 is not.
source: To further test whether this predicted interaction between C457, C459, D248, and H249 was vital to viral replication, we mutated either D248 or H249 to alanine in the Kc1/p6 Gluc replicon and quantified Gluc expression 4 d.p.t. D248 was dispensable for viral replication while H249 is not Figure 5—figure supplement 1
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: D248 is variable across all eight known HEV genotypes while H249 is highly conserved.
source: D248 is variable across all eight known HEV genotypes while H249 is highly conserved (Figure 5B).
evidence: The claim is supported by sequence alignment data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Mutating C483A, C563A, or H249A are predicted to cause regions of the methyltransferase, helicase, and RdRp to reconfigure.
source: Mutating C483A, C563A, or H249A are predicted to cause regions of the methyltransferase, helicase, and RdRp to reconfigure (Figure 5A, right; Videos 3 and 4, 6 respectively).
evidence: The claim is supported by AlphaFold structural predictions shown in Figure 5A and Videos 3, 4, and 6.

claim: Mutating C563A, D248A, or H249A causes a predicted membrane association domain that is exposed in the WT ORF1 protein to become buried.
source: Furthermore, mutating C563A, D248A, or H249A causes a predicted membrane association domain that is exposed in the WT ORF1 protein to become buried, possibly preventing the association with intracellular membranes and preventing/hindering the formation of a replication compartment (Metzger et al., 2022; Szkolnicka et al., 2019; Videos 4–6, respectively).
evidence: The claim is supported by AlphaFold structural predictions shown in Videos 4-6, with citations to Metzger et al., 2022 and Szkolnicka et al., 2019.

claim: By interfering with divalent metal ion binding domains within the pPCP, structural domains vital to viral replication form aberrantly, and prevent HEV ORF1 from efficiently replicating.
source: Taken together, these results suggest that by interfering with divalent metal ion binding domains within the pPCP, structural domains vital to viral replication form aberrantly, and prevent HEV ORF1 from efficiently replicating.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the structural predictions and replication data.

claim: Regions within ORF1 are predicted to harbor Ca2+ and Zn2+ ion binding sites.
source: Outside of our own analysis that suggests the pPCP of HEV ORF1 has metal ion binding activity, other groups have identified regions within ORF1 predicted to harbor Ca2+ and Zn2+ ion binding sites (Parvez and Khan, 2014; Proudfoot et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Parvez and Khan, 2014 and Proudfoot et al., 2019.

claim: Across all mutants, none were able to bind zinc ion species as well as the WT ORF1, save the Pol(-) RdRp mutant.
source: We found that across all mutants, none were able to bind zinc ion species as well as the WT ORF1, save the Pol(-) RdRp mutant, lending validity to our structural hypotheses generated with AlphaFold.
evidence: The claim is supported by ICP-MS experimental data.

claim: The C483A mutation loses ORF1 nuclear localization.
source: Utilizing confocal microscopy, we were able to demonstrate that the C483A mutation loses ORF1 nuclear localization
evidence: The claim is supported by confocal microscopy data.

claim: The H249A mutation decreases nuclear localization of ORF1, and prevents puncta formation throughout the cytoplasm.
source: while the H249A mutation decreases nuclear localization of ORF1, and prevents puncta formation throughout the cytoplasm, which lies in stark contrast to WT ORF1.
evidence: The claim is supported by confocal microscopy data.

claim: HEV ORF1 likely functions as one large multidomain protein that does not undergo proteolytic processing.
source: Taken together, our work demonstrates that HEV ORF1 likely functions as one large multidomain protein that does not undergo proteolytic processing
evidence: The claim is inferred from the transcomplementation experiments and structural analyses.

claim: The putative catalytic residues predicted by prior bioinformatic analyses are actually structural in nature via their ability to bind divalent metal ions.
source: and that the putative catalytic residues predicted by prior bioinformatic analyses are actually structural in nature via their ability to bind divalent metal ions.
evidence: The claim is supported by ICP-MS data, structural predictions, and mutagenesis experiments.

claim: HEV ORF1 operates as a multifunctional protein, which is not subject to proteolytic processing.
source: Our data show that ORF1 operates as a multifunctional protein, which is not subject to proteolytic processing.
evidence: The claim is stated in the abstract as a conclusion from the study's data.

claim: Six cysteines within the pPCP domain are essential for viral replication.
source: Supporting this model, scanning mutagenesis performed on the putative papain-like cysteine protease (pPCP) domain revealed six cysteines essential for viral replication.
evidence: The claim is stated in the abstract as a result from scanning mutagenesis experiments.

claim: The six essential cysteines play a role in divalent metal ion coordination, which governs local and interdomain interactions that are critical for the overall structure of ORF1.
source: Our data are consistent with their role in divalent metal ion coordination, which governs local and interdomain interactions that are critical for the overall structure of ORF1
evidence: The claim is stated in the abstract as a conclusion consistent with the study's data.

claim: The 'pPCP' domain can only rescue viral genome replication in trans when expressed in the context of the full-length ORF1 protein but not as an individual subdomain.
source: furthermore, the 'pPCP' domain can only rescue viral genome replication in trans when expressed in the context of the full-length ORF1 protein but not as an individual subdomain.
evidence: The claim is stated in the abstract as a result from transcomplementation experiments.

claim: Cells expressing ORF1 WT-HA showed significant expression of ORF1 in both the cytoplasm and nucleus.
source: Cells expressing ORF1 WT-HA showed significant expression of ORF1 in both the cytoplasm and nucleus as previously reported (Metzger et al., 2022) and showed many puncta aggregates throughout the cytoplasm (Figure 7).
evidence: The claim is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 7, with citation to Metzger et al., 2022.

claim: Cells expressing ORF1 WT-HA showed many puncta aggregates throughout the cytoplasm.
source: Cells expressing ORF1 WT-HA showed significant expression of ORF1 in both the cytoplasm and nucleus as previously reported (Metzger et al., 2022) and showed many puncta aggregates throughout the cytoplasm (Figure 7).
evidence: The claim is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 7.

claim: The replication deficient ORF1 C483A-HA expressing cells lost the ability for ORF1 to localize to the nucleus and was found dispersed throughout the cytoplasm.
source: In contrast, the replication deficient ORF1 C483A-HA expressing cells lost the ability for ORF1 to localize to the nucleus and was found dispersed throughout the cytoplasm (Figure 7).
evidence: The claim is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 7.

claim: Cells expressing the C563A-HA mutant of ORF1 showed similar localization patterns to ORF1 WT-HA, with puncta forming in the cytoplasm and maintaining the ability to localize to the nucleus.
source: Cells expressing the C563A-HA mutant of ORF1 showed similar localization patterns to ORF1 WT-HA, with puncta forming in the cytoplasm and maintaining the ability to localize to the nucleus (Figure 7).
evidence: The claim is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 7.

claim: Replication competent ORF1 D248A-HA shared localization patterns with ORF1 WT-HA, forming cytoplasmic puncta and localizing within the nucleus.
source: Replication competent ORF1 D248A-HA, like C563A-HA, shared localization patterns with ORF1 WT-HA, forming cytoplasmic puncta and localizing within the nucleus (Figure 7).
evidence: The claim is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 7.

claim: Replication deficient ORF1 H249A-HA showed very disperse cytoplasmic localization, no aggregate formation, and a lesser ability to localize to the nucleus.
source: In contrast, replication deficient ORF1 H249A-HA showed very disperse cytoplasmic localization, no aggregate formation, and a lesser ability to localize to the nucleus (Figure 7).
evidence: The claim is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 7.

claim: Localization of ORF1 seems to correlate with replicative capacity, with nuclear localization being lost or diminished in mutants that cannot replicate.
source: Taken together with the replication data of these epitope-tagged ORF1 mutants (Figure 5—figure supplement 1), localization of ORF1 seems to correlate with replicative capacity, with nuclear localization being lost or diminished in mutants that cannot replicate (C483A-HA and H249A-HA), and mutants able to establish replication (C563A-HA and D248A-HA) share localization patterns with ORF1 WT-HA.
evidence: The claim is inferred from comparing localization patterns with replication data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1 and Figure 7.

claim: Mutants able to establish replication (C563A-HA and D248A-HA) share localization patterns with ORF1 WT-HA.
source: Taken together with the replication data of these epitope-tagged ORF1 mutants (Figure 5—figure supplement 1), localization of ORF1 seems to correlate with replicative capacity, with nuclear localization being lost or diminished in mutants that cannot replicate (C483A-HA and H249A-HA), and mutants able to establish replication (C563A-HA and D248A-HA) share localization patterns with ORF1 WT-HA.
evidence: The claim is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 7 and replication data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: HCV utilizes a metalloprotein in its replicase, the nonstructural protein NS5A.
source: For instance, HCV utilizes a metalloprotein in its replicase, the nonstructural protein NS5A (Tellinghuisen et al., 2004; Tellinghuisen et al., 2005)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Tellinghuisen et al., 2004 and Tellinghuisen et al., 2005.

claim: HCV utilizes four cysteines within a C[x]17CxC[x]20C motif, conserved among Hepacivirus and Pestivirus genera, for Zn2+ coordination and proper function of the HCV replicase machinery.
source: HCV utilizes four cysteines within a C[x]17CxC[x]20C motif, conserved among Hepacivirus and Pestivirus genera, for Zn2+ coordination and proper function of the HCV replicase machinery.
evidence: The claim is stated as established knowledge about HCV.

claim: While each mutant is heterogenous with each other in binding activity for most divalent ions, all mutations within the pPCP bind less Zn2+ than WT.
source: Element signatures indicate that while each mutant is heterogenous with each other in binding activity for most divalent ions, all mutations within the pPCP bind less Zn2+ than WT.
evidence: The claim is supported by ICP-MS experimental data.

claim: The element signature for the Pol (-) mutant bound all elements similar to WT.
source: Unsurprisingly, the element signature for the Pol (-) mutant bound all elements similar to WT (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by ICP-MS experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Divalent ion binding capacity likely affects proper structural confirmation of ORF1, leading to differential replication capacity based on mutation position.
source: These results suggest that divalent ion binding capacity likely affects proper structural confirmation of ORF1, leading to differential replication capacity based on mutation position.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the ICP-MS data showing differential ion binding and replication data.

claim: Most characterized (+) ssRNA viruses rely on proteases to liberate individual gene products from their encoded polyprotein.
source: While most characterized (+) ssRNA viruses rely on proteases to liberate individual gene products from their encoded polyprotein, HEV may be an exception.
evidence: The claim is stated as established knowledge about (+) ssRNA viruses.

claim: HEV may be an exception to most characterized (+) ssRNA viruses that rely on proteases to liberate individual gene products from their encoded polyprotein.
source: While most characterized (+) ssRNA viruses rely on proteases to liberate individual gene products from their encoded polyprotein, HEV may be an exception.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the study's findings about ORF1 function.

claim: The inability for the putative HEV PCP to act outside of the context of the FL ORF1 protein suggests that it has some orthogonal activity and that HEV ORF1 likely functions as one large multi-domain protein.
source: The inability for the putative HEV PCP to act outside of the context of the FL ORF1 protein suggests that it has some orthogonal activity and that HEV ORF1 likely functions as one large multi-domain protein.
